ModMetaData.name: AgentTouchFix
ModMetaData.author: SleepSheepQwQ
ModMetaData.description:
Runtime Harmony fixes for the Android touch port (Waylith engine), no vanilla DLL is modified.
1) Developer tools (LudeonTK DebugTools) work with touch. The port turns every map tap into a synthetic selection (PortUI.MobileSelectionController.Tap) and never produces the MouseDown that DebugTool.DebugToolOnGUI needs, so an armed tool never fires and the tap is stolen by the selector. - PortUI.MobileSelectionController.Tap is skipped while a tool is armed; the tool's clickAction is invoked instead, with UI.MouseCell() and UI.MouseMapPosition() pinned to the tapped target. - The tap is snapped through PortUI's own candidate picker (MobileSelectionController.Candidates: the exact cell first, then the 5x5 surrounding cells within a 28.8 px screen radius, nearest first), so a tap does not have to land exactly on the entity. Empty ground keeps the raw tap coordinate, unrounded. - Long press cancels the armed tool (touch equivalent of the right mouse button). - RimWorld.Selector.HandleMapClicks is skipped while a tool is armed (real mouse fallback) and a half-open drag box is disarmed so selection can never "stick". - LudeonTK.DebugTool.DebugToolOnGUI is suppressed on the frame a tool already fired through the touch path, so a real mouse event cannot fire the same tool twice.
2) Pointer no longer sticks after a two finger gesture, and a one finger drag no longer turns into a zoom. - Ports1de.TouchGestureEngine.SecondUp leaves state = Ignore and no branch of Move()/Up() handles Ignore, so the finger still on the screen emits nothing until it is lifted and pressed again. The postfix forces state = Idle and drops the pinch baseline / inertia. - RwHost.TouchControls.OnTouch: on ACTION_POINTER_UP / ACTION_CANCEL the engine and the GameCamera accumulators are reset, and the remaining finger is re-armed as a pan (or the remaining two fingers as a pinch) so the gesture continues instead of dying. - Stale GameCamera pan/zoom accumulators are cleared at gesture end, which removes the "leftover zoom applied on the next frame" effect.
3) Silent by default (v5). Nothing is written to the in-game log window, so the game no longer pops the "there were errors / warnings" dialog. - Every line goes to files/game/agenttouchfix.log (rotated at 1 MB, one previous file kept). - Optional diagnostics: create an empty file files/game/agenttouchfix.diag next to it and restart. The touch/camera diagnostics are then re-enabled and INFO lines are additionally mirrored to the in-game console (Log.Message only - never Warning/Error). Delete the file to go quiet again. The flag is read once, at startup. - Runtime failures (a tap or a gesture) are file-only; only a patch that fails to apply at startup reports once, in game.
4) Snapping is hit tested (v6). A tapped map position is only snapped onto a Thing when the tap really aimed at it: inside the thing's own footprint, or within 16 dp (and never more than half a cell) of its projected screen position. A tap on empty ground next to an item now stays on the empty cell, which is what terrain / spawn tools need. With nothing under the tap and a single thing selected, the selected thing is used instead (tools that answer to the selection). Switch (read once at startup), files/game/agenttouchfix.snap: auto (default, also used when the file is absent) - the hit test above always - old behaviour: snap to the nearest candidate no matter how far the tap was off - never snap; the exact tapped cell and position are used This switch governs the developer-tool path only (an armed LudeonTK tool firing on a map tap). Ordinary map taps are answered by PortUI's own candidate picker - see item 10 for that one.
5) Tooltips no longer stick to the touch point (v9). The real cause was the virtual cursor: the port's tap path calls Click(), which pushes the cursor position onto the tapped button and never moves it away, so Verse.TooltipHandler sees Mouse.IsOver(rect) forever, re-registers the tip every frame and keeps the hover highlight on. After the last finger leaves the screen the cursor is now pushed off screen (RwHost.Native.glfwAndroidPushCursorPos(-1, -1)), so the tip disappears on release, like it does with a real mouse. Switch (read once at startup), files/game/agenttouchfix.tips: park (default, also used when the file is absent) - move the cursor off screen on release, plus the TipRegion suppression below as a second line of defence suppress - only the TipRegion suppression, the cursor is never moved off - neither: the patches stay installed and return immediately TooltipHandler.TipRegion / TipRegionByKey are skipped while the finger is the last input device (up to 2 s after it left), a deliberate hold of 500 ms or more shows the description, and after such a hold the tip stays allowed for another 800 ms so it does not blink. On desktop, or with a real mouse being moved, nothing changes. A skipped tooltip never calls Event.current.Use().
6) Double tapping a building selects every one of that kind on screen (v7). PortUI.MobileSelectionController.Tap only had a multi-select branch for ThingCategory.Item, so a double tap on a wall or a workbench just re-selected the single building. A second tap on the same building within 400 ms is now handled by the mod: it pins UI.MouseCell()/UI.MouseMapPosition() to the building and calls the vanilla Selector.SelectAllMatchingObjectUnderMouseOnScreen(), which is what a desktop double click does. The current selection is not cleared first.
7) Text typed with the Android keyboard is no longer dropped, which is what made Chinese input look broken (v7). Ports1de.TextEditMailbox.TryTake() compared the whole TextEditTarget - window id, keyboard control id and the field rect - so any layout change between opening the editor and the IME answering (a scrolled window, a re-laid-out dialog, the keyboard resizing the screen) threw the text away. When the exact match fails, a pending answer from the same window is delivered instead: exactly once, and only if it has not expired. Both sides must report the same window id, and when there is no window at all (id -1) the keyboard control id has to match as well.
8) Mouse buttons and keys are released when the app loses the input device (v8). The host forwards input to the engine and keeps its own mirror of what is held, but it clears that mirror on surface destroy, configuration change and focus loss without forwarding a release - and OnPause does not even clear it - so the engine kept a button pressed whose release was never sent (the mirror and the engine then agree on "nothing is held", and no later event ever corrects it). The same lifecycle events now release every held mouse button first. OnPause also resets the mirror, which that method never did, so the next press is not swallowed. Keyboard pushes had no bookkeeping at all, so a held key (WASD, Shift) stayed down after focus loss / pause / surface recreation and the pawn kept walking. Presses are now tracked by scan code and the missing releases are sent from the same four lifecycle methods. KEYCODE_BACK is not tracked: it maps to Escape and OnBackPressed already sends its own press+release pair.
9) Lifting one mouse button no longer releases the others (v8). RwHost clears every held button whenever an ACTION_UP arrives. On devices that report the still held buttons in that event, a button the player never released was let go, and the following move event pressed it again - a phantom click / a broken drag. Now only the button that actually went up is released, exactly as the port already does for a second button on a pointer-up; the ordinary single button release is handled by the unmodified game code.
10) A tap on empty ground no longer jumps to the nearest entity (v10). The tap is not the mod's: PortUI.MobileSelectionController.Candidates answers a tap with what is on that cell and, when the cell holds nothing, additionally scans the 5x5 cells around it and inserts everything within 28.8 px of the finger in front of the cell's own contents, nearest first. That radius search is what the player feels as "I tapped the ground and it grabbed the item / pawn next to it". Switch (read once at startup), files/game/agenttouchfix.pick: port (default, also used when the file is absent) - untouched, exactly as shipped exact - when the tapped cell itself holds no selectable Thing, that radius search is skipped and the candidate list is just what is really on the cell (usually nothing), so the tap stays where the finger was. A cell that does hold something is handled by the original method, unchanged. The switch touches only that one branch: it never rewrites arguments and never bypasses the original in the branch it does not own. Log: `pick mode=exact skipped-radius=N` (at most one line per 2 s) plus the startup line `pick mode=<mode> (...)`. Independent of the developer-tool snapping in item 4: an armed tool still snaps onto the entity under the finger, which is what makes terrain and spawn tools usable.
11) Read-only texture counters for the grey / flickering / scrambled texture fault (v10). A diagnostic build cannot fix that fault blind, so this version counts what the texture paths actually do. Every one of these patches only reads and increments - no argument is changed, no result is written, and no governor / memory method is patched. - Ports1de.DdsFallback.TryPlan: the decoded-texture budget and maxDimension the caller asked for, and (postfix) the plan's Format / Width / Height / Shift / SourceMip. - Ports1de.DdsFallback.TryConvert: whether the software decode succeeded and how many bytes the converted DDS took (used). If the plan postfix cannot be installed, the mip shift is derived from the input vs. converted pixel width instead. - Waylith.Rendering.Texture2D.Evict, GpuTextureService.GetOrCreateFallbackTexture, TextureResidency.Offload and TextureResidency.EvictHostResident: how often a texture is evicted, how often the 1x1 stand-in colour is handed out, and how often residency moves textures out or evicts the host-resident copies. Every 30 s one line is appended to files/game/agenttouchfix.log (file only, never Verse.Log): tex: decode ok=N shift>0=N fail=N fallback=N evict=N offload=N budget=<MiB> limit=<px> hostevict=N plus one detail line the first time a down-shifted plan appears and the first time a decode fails (format code, input size, shift, budget, limit). The patch summary line `tex: probes ok=.. skipped=.. failed=..` says whether the counters could be installed at all.
12) Automatic texture eviction can be held back for textures that are in use (v11). The v10 counters showed the texture fault is eviction, not the decoded-texture budget: in one minute at 256 MiB and a 4096 px limit not a single mip was reduced, yet about 120 textures per second were thrown away. The port queues every texture that has a SourcePath for eviction (Texture2D.EvictWhenCached) and every frame evicts whatever is queued as soon as the disk cache holds a copy (DrainPendingEvictions -> Texture2D.Evict), without asking whether that texture is on screen. A texture evicted in the frame it is drawn samples the 1x1 fallback colour, and while it re-hydrates only part of the mip chain is back - the panel-background plus incomplete-texture picture. files/game/agenttouchfix.texkeep selects how much of that is suppressed: grace (default, also when the file is absent) - the eviction is skipped in two cases: a) small textures: GpuResource.AllocatedBytes is at or below the byte count in files/game/agenttouchfix.texsmall (default 1048576 = 1 MiB, 0 disables the rule). Icons and small UI bits are single small textures - evicting one only buys a reload of the same bytes the next time it is drawn, and a few thousand of them resident is tens of MiB. b) hot textures: GpuTextureService.RenderFrameSerial - GpuResource.LastUseFrame is below the frame count in files/game/agenttouchfix.texgrace (default 900 frames = 15 s at 60 fps, clamped to 60..3600). A cold large texture is still evicted exactly as shipped, so the resident set cannot grow without bound. on - EvictWhenCached and DrainPendingEvictions are both short-circuited, i.e. every texture stays resident. This is the control case for the experiment, not a default. off - no eviction method is patched at all; the port behaves exactly as shipped. Log: `texkeep mode=grace grace=900 small=1.0MiB skipped=hot:N,small:N evicted=N` (at most one line per 2 s) plus the startup line that names the mode, both windows and which targets were patched. Only those eviction entry points are patched: Texture2D.Dispose / DisposeMovedAway / TryEvictForResidency / EnsureResident, the upload path, TextureResidency.Offload / EvictHostResident and the memory governor are untouched, and when the frame/usage numbers cannot be read the gate lets every eviction through (one Warn, never a blocked eviction).
Nothing under RwHost.AndroidMemoryAndGcGovernor is patched, and no texture or memory path is written (v9, unchanged in v10 and v11 apart from the v11 eviction gate in item 12): the grey / flickering / scrambled textures came from the port itself (quality tier falling to Economy, a small decoded-texture budget, BC sampling through software decode), not from the mod. The v10 texture patches are read-only counters installed to prove exactly that.
Everything is registered with AccessTools and fails soft: a missing target is recorded in the log file and the rest of the patches stay active. Nothing is patched permanently outside these methods.
Requires the mobile port (PortUI/RwHost present). Harmless on desktop RimWorld: the touch-only patches are simply skipped.
